theme_and_runs.why: Unmistakably a mini-game (goal, turn/loop limits, win and lose states, per-level bests, 5-10 minute sessions) and it runs spotlessly: all 25 automated checks pass, no console errors or warnings, no horizontal scroll at 320/375/1440, playable with localStorage throwing, refused moves cost no turn, and the lose state offers Retry and Back to levels; I independently re-implemented the engine and confirmed all six levels are solvable inside par and the turn limit and that none can be reached without entering a door tile, but level 3 is content-broken (see below) and every rewind respawns you on top of your parked ghosts, quietly breaking the 'bodies never share a tile' rule the prompt called the specification.

originality.why: Record-your-past-self-as-a-co-op-ghost with pressure plates and doors is not on the banned-clone list and is nicely framed, but it is a well-established puzzle genre developers will recognise (Chronotron / Time Bandit / the recurring jam staple) implemented straight, with no twist layered on top - despite the title nothing paradoxical ever happens, ghosts only block and press, so the idea is competent-familiar rather than new.

ux_design.why: Coherent dark palette from custom properties, colour plus shape (circle vs diamond) for the two door colours, CSS-illustrated three-step tutorial with a legend, level select with locks and em-dash bests, real buttons at 46px, D-pad plus swipe plus keyboard, visible focus rings, inert-and-Tab-trapped modals, and a board aria-label that narrates the full state; held off a 5 because the mobile breakpoint hides the entire side card so phone players lose the level hint and ghost list, reduced-motion nulls the bump animation that is the only visual signal of a refused move, level 1 greets you with '0 LOOPS LEFT' in warning red, and nothing anywhere explains that a ghost you block loses a turn off its whole timeline - a lag that is mandatory to solve levels 4 to 6.

prompt_quality.why: Genuinely thoughtful about an unsupervised agent - it specifies behaviour not code, names the traps (file:// module ban, missing doctype and quirks mode, storage that throws, listeners in a loop, use-before-definition), and demands the agent actually solve every level and prove the doors are load-bearing, which visibly worked; docked because section 8's checklist is almost pure restatement of sections 5 and 7, and because the prompt contradicts itself - its own door rule ('open while at least one plate of its colour is occupied') makes level 3's brief ('two plates of the same colour... needs two ghosts') impossible, and the agent faithfully shipped the contradiction.

reproducibility.why: Rules, control map, screen list, level count and teaching order, and technical constraints are pinned down hard enough that a rerun would almost certainly yield the same runnable game with the same key features; only the exact layouts are left open, and the required solvability proof is the expensive step most likely to be skipped under a 60-minute clock, so layout quality (and worst case an unsolvable room) is the real run-to-run variance.

key_features_a_rerun_must_reproduce: Single offline index.html with a turn-based grid puzzle where Rewind resets the room and spawns a ghost that literally replays your previous attempt beside you, with a per-loop turn limit and a loop limit (par)
Two colours of pressure plate holding matching doors open while any body stands on them, with refused moves (wall, shut door, occupied tile) costing no turn
Six hand-designed levels in the stated teaching order, each solvable within its par and turn limit and none reachable without opening a door
Full screen set - title, how to play, level select with locks and bests, playing with a status bar, paused, level complete, out of loops, and an all-levels ending
Keyboard, on-screen buttons and swipe all working, plus localStorage bests that degrade silently to in-memory when storage throws
biggest_weakness: Level 3 'Two Plates' does not teach what it claims and is redundant: because a door opens when at least ONE plate of its colour is occupied, its second plate is decorative, and I verified it falls to a single ghost in 2 loops (10 turns) under a par of 3 - identical in every way to level 2, so one sixth of the campaign is a wasted rung on the difficulty ladder and the level's own name is a lie.
single_highest_leverage_fix: Make multi-plate doors require ALL plates of their colour to be held at once (or redesign level 3 around two doors that must be open simultaneously), and fix the prompt's matching contradiction between its 'at least one plate' door rule and its 'needs two ghosts' brief for level 3.
